title: Stability seeding log (personal notes)
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for the next small rollout (we're calling this a 'seeding' phase rather than a canary). Goal is low-friction verification of latency/cost/quality under production traffic without affecting steady-state client SLAs.
- Target model: rwd-2b-v3-quant (pinned for this experiment).
- Customer cohorts: internal infra tests + 3 low-risk beta customers (cohort ids: beta-a, beta-b, beta-c).

Primary objectives (what I want to learn):
1) Verify steady-state p95 tail under mixed prompt length distribution (0-1.5k tokens).
2) Confirm no tokenization/regression causing hallucination spike on our evaluation prompts.
3) Exercise fallback path (model variant fallback) under simulated GPU pressure.

Hypotheses:
- If we seed at low qps with slow ramp and run for 48h, p95 will stay <= 220ms for short prompts and <= 750ms for long prompts.
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate will > 35% for the beta cohorts after warmup.
- No quality regressions (eval pass rate drop < 2 percentage points).

Seeding plan (stepwise):
- PRE: push pinned image tag to staging and validate smoke (unit tests + short latency bench) — owner: me (Uma).
- STEP 0 (internal): 10 qps total, 100% internal traffic, 1h. Check basic telemetry, logs, memory.
- STEP 1 (beta-a): route 0.1% of beta-a traffic (expected ~2 qps), duration 4h.
- STEP 2 (beta-b): 0.5% beta-b, add in after STEP 1 stable for 2h.
- STEP 3 (beta-c + internal): 1% beta-c + internal soak, 24h.
- STEP 4 (scaling test): synthetic ramp to 5x observed qps for 10 minutes to trigger fallback; verify fallback path correctness.
- EXIT: either promote to gradual rollout or pin rollback depending on metrics.

Traffic split guidance (manual ramps):
- Use route-level flags in console: create route tag "seed-ux-2026-02" and set percentages.
- Remember client affinity: schedule small window when clients are less active (UTC 03:00-07:00).

Pinning and version notes:
- Pin config: model: rwd-2b-v3-quant@2026-02-25-rc3
- Engine image: runtime:v1.18.4-seed
- Config snippet to apply (kubectl/helm style):
  - MODEL_PIN=rwd-2b-v3-quant@2026-02-25-rc3
  - RUNTIME_IMAGE=runtime:v1.18.4-seed
  - ROLLOUT_LABEL=seed-ux-2026-02

Safety checks (hard stop thresholds):
- Latency p95 short prompts > 350ms OR p95 long prompts > 1050ms -> pause and scale down to internal-only.
- Error rate (5xx or runtime-exec errors) > 0.8% sustained over 5m -> immediate rollback to previous pinned variant.
- Increase in non-deterministic responses (eval failure delta > 4pp) -> rollback and open SR with model-ops.

Telemetry to watch (dashboard names / metrics):
- Dashboard: "seed-ux-2026-02 / latency & errors"
- Metrics: client_qps, p50/p95/p99 latency broken by prompt-length-bucket, token_cost_per_request, kv_cache_hit_rate, prompt_eval_pass_rate
- Traces: sample traces for any p95 spikes; include full prompt -> response payload in trace when investigating quality regressions (PII scrubbed).

Fallback / rollforward playbook (commands / steps):
- Immediate: reduce route percentage to 0% for route tag via Console or API: POST /routes/{route}/adjust -> {percent:0} (auth: ops-key)
- If latency errors tied to GPU eviction: scale down to 0 and route internal only, notify SRE to inspect node pool.
- If quality regression: pin back to rwd-2b-v2-stable and create ticket INF-XXXX (capture failure prompts).

Quick checklist before STEP 0 (preflight):
- [ ] Confirm pinned model artifact uploaded and SHA verified.
- [ ] Publish route tag seed-ux-2026-02 in Console.
- [ ] Notify beta customers + Slack channel #infra-seeding (message template ready).
- [ ] Confirm alerting thresholds wired to on-call (pagerduty).

Open questions / investigation items (notes to self):
- Need to re-evaluate cold-start for KV caches with v3 quant; current cache warmup heuristics may be conservative. Could we pre-warm with synthetic prefix traffic? Action: ask research (Priya) for warmup tool.
- How will billing attribution appear for these tiny seeded percentages? Confirm with finance whether internal test costs are billed to infra dev budget or product credits. Jorge to check.
- Decide if we should enable continuous fallback telemetry (log fallback events) for the whole seeding window — good for post-mortem.

After-action (placeholders for notes post-seed):
- 2026-03-xx: jot observed p95, cache hit rates, any regressions, and whether we promoted.

Random friction notes (things I forgot last time):
- Console label creation sometimes needs org-admin permission; pre-check roles on my account.
- Clients with older SDKs might not respect route tags; have a fallback verification that clients report route header.

TL;DR personal summary (one-liner):
Seed small, watch latency & evals, keep rollback easy. If any safety threshold trips, cut to internal-only and diagnose.

-- end of scratchpad --
(Will copy relevant bits into a tidy Confluence page if seeding goes green)
